name: Gomer
overview: Gomer is a male figure identified as a son of Japheth, one of Noah's sons, according to Genesis 10:2. His lineage places him among the descendants of Noah, highlighting his role in the genealogical record of the nations. There are no additional notes or tribal affiliations recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Gomer means 'complete' and is used as a proper name in Scripture. This meaning is provided in the context of Genesis 10:2 and does not indicate that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Gomer is the son of Japheth. He is also the father of three sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah, as explicitly stated in Genesis 10:3. These relationships situate Gomer within the broader genealogical framework of the nations descending from Noah.
scriptureSignificance: Gomer's significance lies primarily in his position within the genealogical account of Genesis, where he represents one of the foundational ancestors of various peoples. His descendants, named in the following verse, contribute to the understanding of the dispersion and multiplication of nations after the flood. While not central to a narrative event, Gomer's role as a progenitor underscores God's sovereign plan in populating the earth through Noah's family.
